problem:
Several egg cartons were checked for cracked eggs. The number of cracked eggs in each carton was recorded below. If $N$ is the number of cracked eggs in a carton, what is the expected value of $N?$

| Number of Cartons | $10$ | $7$ | $2$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cracked Eggs | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |

activity_context.topic_title: Expected Values of Discrete Random Variables

feedback.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Let $X$ be the value shown on a randomly spun spinner. Then the support is $S={2,4,6,8}.$

On the spinner there are $1$ section labeled with two, $2$ sections labeled with four, $3$ sections labeled with six, and $4$ sections labeled with eight (ten sections in total), so the probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2) & =\frac{1}{10} \\ P(4) & =\frac{2}{10}=\frac{1}{5} \\ P(6) & =\frac{3}{10} \\ P(8) & =\frac{4}{10}=\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =2\cdot f(2)+4\cdot f(4)+6\cdot f(6)+8\cdot f(8) \\  & =2(\frac{1}{10})+4(\frac{1}{5})+6(\frac{3}{10})+8(\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =\frac{2}{10}+\frac{4}{5}+\frac{18}{10}+\frac{16}{5} \\  & =\frac{2}{10}+\frac{8}{10}+\frac{18}{10}+\frac{32}{10} \\  & =\frac{2+8+18+32}{10} \\  & =\frac{60}{10} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
